sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark (fill in the blanks, true/false, match the columns or one word).

questions.q: Fill in the blanks. (a) The tourist expects the tour to be organised as per the ________ mentioned in the tour package. (b) Railneer bottled water is a product of ________.

Fill in the blanks. (a) It was only in ________ that a separate Ministry of Tourism and Civil Aviation was created under a Cabinet Minister. (b) The forerunner of the cheque, the Circular Note, was created in ________.
Expand the following. (a) FIT (b) CRS.
questions.answer: (a) Foreign Independent Travel (Free Individual Traveller). (b) Computer Reservation System.

questions.q: True or False. (a) Travel agencies should be truthful in marketing and publicity. (b) IRCTC was incorporated in 1989.
Fill in the blanks. (a) CSR stands for Corporate ________ Responsibility. (b) A visa is an endorsement on a ________.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Why is Corporate Social Responsibility important for travel agencies? (two points)
questions.answer: It ensures their activities do not harm local people and communities. It helps destination sustainability through training, school amenities and empowerment.

questions.q: What is meant by FAM tour? Why is it conducted?
questions.answer: FAM is a familiarisation tour. It is conducted to check the feasibility of an itinerary or package and as a promotional method with destination promoters.

questions.q: What is a visa?
questions.answer: A visa is an endorsement on a passport that allows the holder to enter, leave or stay in a country for a specified period.

questions.q: State two uses of travel insurance.
questions.answer: It gives security for personal and baggage losses. It covers life, accident, medical treatment and trip cancellation losses.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Why is corporate social responsibility important? Explain in three points.
questions.answer: (i) Business should make a direct positive contribution to society. (ii) It supports training, basic amenities in government schools and empowerment of women. (iii) Destination sustainability is possible only when all stakeholders take social responsibility.

questions.q: Explain any three functions of a travel agency (from this lesson).
questions.answer: (i) Marketing and publicity of packages and destinations. (ii) Reservation of tickets, hotel rooms and ground services. (iii) Travel information, document processing, insurance and currency exchange.

questions.q: Explain the importance of itinerary preparation and package tour design (three points).
questions.answer: (i) Differentiated products help firms survive competition. (ii) Expert teams check feasibility through familiarisation trips. (iii) Costing and launching a package bring revenue and promote tourism.

questions.q: Explain the importance of disaster preparedness for travel agencies (three points).
questions.answer: (i) Safety and security of visitors is the prime responsibility. (ii) Disasters such as floods, earthquakes and terror strikes are uncertain. (iii) Trained teams coordinate with local disaster management teams to prevent harm.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Explain the major functions of travel agencies and tour operators, in six points.
questions.answer: (i) Marketing and publicity of packages, destinations and attractions. (ii) Reservation of tickets, hotel rooms and ground services. (iii) Itinerary preparation, package designing and costing. (iv) Travel information and processing of passport, visa and other documents. (v) Travel insurance, currency exchange and organising MICE events. (vi) Research, training, CSR and disaster preparedness.

questions.q: Explain the travel documents and the formalities travel agents handle for a foreign trip, in six points.
questions.answer: (i) Passport is the basic travel document. (ii) A visa is an endorsement allowing entry and stay for a period. (iii) Health certificates and vaccination are needed. (iv) Travel insurance covers life, baggage and cancellation. (v) Foreign currency is arranged within RBI and FEMA rules. (vi) Agents process these documents to avoid trouble or denied entry.
